stem: After the transfusion is stopped, a 74-year-old client with CKD and compensated heart failure has improving dyspnea after oxygen, upright positioning, and ordered IV furosemide. During the second unit she developed SpO2 89% on room air, BP 168/96, JVD, new S3, worsening 2+ edema, oliguria, and bilateral crackles. Chest X-ray shows pulmonary vascular congestion, small pleural effusions, cardiomegaly, and a widened vascular pedicle. BNP rose from 280 to 890 pg/mL. Complete the bow-tie by selecting the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.

actions.label: A1
actions.text: Maintain high Fowler's position with supplemental oxygen and close respiratory monitoring

actions.label: A2
actions.text: Administer IV fluid bolus to support blood pressure

actions.label: A3
actions.text: Resume the transfusion at a slower rate once SpO2 improves

actions.label: A4
actions.text: Administer ordered IV furosemide and monitor urine output

parameters.label: P2
parameters.text: Temperature trend as the main marker of resolution

parameters.label: P3

parameters.label: P4
